cards.text: This is the Teacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem (Ecclesiastes 1:1). Last chapter, he said the work done under the sun was grievous to him, and that everything is futile, a pursuit of the wind (Ecclesiastes 2:17). Now he starts a new thought about seasons and time, and friend, he is thinking BIG.

cards.question: True or false: the Teacher says only some parts of life get their own season.

cards.text: Then he starts a list, two times to a line, and he opens with the very beginning of a life and the very end of it. No warm-up, no small talk. He goes STRAIGHT to the big one.

cards.question: What's the very first pair of times on the Teacher's list?

answers.text: A time to be born and a time to die
A time to plant and a time to uproot
A time to weep and a time to laugh

cards.text: Next comes a time to plant and a time to uproot, a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to break down and a time to build.

cards.question: Born and die, plant and uproot, break down and build: every time in the Teacher's list comes paired with its ___.

cards.text: Then it gets personal: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance. Friend, I have done all four of those over ONE tray of cookies.

cards.question: The Teacher lists weeping and laughing side by side. True or false: he says only one of them is the right way to live.

cards.text: Then there's a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together. And there's a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing.

cards.question: When the Teacher says there's a time to refrain from embracing, what's he saying about a hug?

answers.text: Even a hug has its time
A hug is always a mistake
A hug is only for family

cards.text: Then comes a time to keep and a time to discard. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer, and that drawer only EVER heard the word keep.

cards.question: Right before that, the Teacher says there's a time to search. True or false: he says there's never a time to give up searching.

cards.text: Then a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak. Friend, I am LOUD, and I am still working on that silent part.

cards.question: The Teacher says there's a time to be silent and a time to speak. What does that tell you about talking?

cards.text: His last line takes on the biggest things of all: love and its opposite, then war and peace.

cards.question: Love shows up in the Teacher's last line along with its opposite. True or false: he says even hate has a time.

cards.text: After that whole list, the Teacher asks one question: "What does the worker gain from his toil?" Friend, that's the same question my snooze button asks me every single morning.

cards.question: Before he answers, the Teacher says he has seen the ___ that God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them.

cards.text: Then he looks back at all those times, the weeping and the dancing, the tearing and the mending. And he says something about how God made every one of them.

cards.question: What does the Teacher say God has made everything, in its time?

cards.text: Then he goes deeper: God has also set eternity in the hearts of men. A heart living by the calendar, and God puts FOREVER inside it.

cards.question: God has set eternity in people's hearts. True or false: the Teacher says people can fathom all of God's work from beginning to end.

cards.text: Last chapter, the Teacher said nothing is better than to eat and drink and enjoy your work, and that this is from the hand of God (Ecclesiastes 2:24). Now he says he knows what's best for people while they live.

cards.question: What does the Teacher say there's nothing better for people to do while they live?

cards.text: He adds that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor. Friend, I spent years in a drawer with NO labor at all, and trust me, the work is the good part.

cards.question: Eating, drinking and finding satisfaction in all your labor? The Teacher calls that the ___ of God.

cards.text: Our times come and go: born and die, plant and uproot. But the Teacher says the things God does are a whole different story.

cards.question: What does the Teacher say about everything God does?
Everything God does endures forever. True or false: the Teacher says people can add to it.
God's work lasts forever, and nothing can be added to it or taken from it. Why does the Teacher say God does it that way?

answers.text: So that people would fear Him
So that people would rest from work
So that kings would rule wisely

cards.text: He ends with this: what exists has already been, and what will be has already been. Kind of like my jokes, friend: even the NEW ones have already been told.

cards.question: True or false: the Teacher says God will call to account what has passed.
